blindSummary: Same-sex conduct is legal in this country, the constitution's equality provisions have been read inclusively, and the capital hosts an annual Pride march with government participation — notable for a young, heavily religious nation. There is no legal gender recognition and services are thin, but there is no documented pattern of police targeting or anti-trans violence, and the small community (two local LGBTQ organisations) operates openly.
blindOutOfScope: Service thinness and the absence of legal gender recognition are resident-facing.
blindSourceSummaries: Aid-corps volunteer programme's Pride guide for this country: country snapshot of the local LGBTQIA+ context - same-sex acts decriminalised in 1975; the 2011 UN Human Rights Council joint statement on SOGI adopted; practical guidance for volunteers on local law, protections and living openly.
A UN health agency's laws-and-policies database filtered to transgender-related laws and policies for this country - database interface showing the legal framework affecting trans people.

A foreign permanent mission's post (March 2011): LGBT rights in the UN context - a major member state's advocacy for SOGI rights at the Human Rights Council, relevant to this country's international human-rights environment.

Overseas politics magazine (June 2018): feature on this country's first Pride parade (2017) - it drew international attention and a televised prime-ministerial endorsement, but the article noted the shine of a single event belied a grittier day-to-day; the organiser received 'gay people are monsters' messages from his own brother - rejection and reconciliation within families.

A foreign public broadcaster (July 2018): the region's youngest nation held its second LGBT pride parade - this country cemented its role as a regional LGBT-rights leader while neighbouring states turn hostile; the prime minister said discrimination, disrespect and abuse toward people because of their sexual orientation or gender identity brought no benefit to the nation.

LGBTQ news outlet (July 2019): this country celebrated its third LGBTQI Pride - ~3,000 people joined a 'diversity march' in the capital, six times the 2017 turnout; the president described himself as a president for all people and asked everyone to see diversity as the nation's wealth; homosexuality legal since 1975.
